title: What characterized Bunk's style: tone, inventiveness, countermelody
summary: Blumberg says Bunk's tone and element of surprise can't be fully captured on records, and whistles his countermelody on Honeysuckle Rose.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: has a lot to do with his tone and his inventiveness, which you can only get a certain amount from records because a lot of it has to do with the element of surprise, and after you've heard a record once, you're no longer surprised by it.
Yeah, but didn't some of the aspects not come down on records?
Yeah, but those are the same things that you just can't put into words.
Well, you could hum some of those countermelodies, for example, like Honeysuckle Rose you said was really exquisite or something like that.
Yeah, he had a very good countermelody on that. I guess I could probably whistle a little better. Let's see.
Let's see. That was a general thing, then he went into the release and so forth.
Did he play the release pretty straight?
Yeah, yeah. The rest of it was pretty straight. That was the theme of his countermelody on it.
Could you do it again, whistle it again? I want to hold the mic around here a little closer. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. .
Just something like that. But I thought it was kind of unusual. Sounds a little bit like the Lenny Tristano school or something. It was surprising to hear in that style.
